title: Constant strict towers and normalized derived direct image

proof.text: Construct quotient transitions and augmentation through scalar-extension adjunctions. The tensor-section formula for the scalar adjunction unit, linearity, and the sheafification tensor-generator extensionality prove naturality, strict transition compatibility and uniqueness. Obtain the universal reduction model from the resolving class of K-flat complexes. Its generic four-field record is specialized to the same reduction functor and K-flat predicate; this changes representation only.

Use the canonical right-derived composition comparisons to define the diagonal/direct-image square. Their universal-unit factorization proves its formula on K-injectives. Evaluation and the ordinary constant-square mate identify the evaluated comparison with the identity. The diagonal/limit unit is invertible by fully faithful derived diagonal. The conjugate-adjunction unit equation and the diagonal square mate prove the inverse-limit normalization.

At each quotient level, conjugate the sectionwise identity restriction/direct-image comparison through the extension-of-scalars and inverse-image adjunctions. Compose with the canonical restriction/pullback isomorphism. The conjugate-unit identity gives the image of 1 tensor x, and scalar linearity gives the stated formula for every s tensor x. Naturality of constant coefficient maps and the characterized quotient transition give compatibility of successive levels. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles the strict tower map; its levelwise isomorphisms make it an isomorphism. Adjunction and tensor-generator extensionality prove uniqueness.

Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions whose inverse images remain K-flat. The algebraic presentation of the specified pro-etale inverse image supplies the hypotheses of ringed-topos K-flat pullback. On their homotopy images both reduction counits are invertible. The ordinary square and these counits give an invertible comparison on this full resolving class. Extend it by the right-fraction resolving-class theorem, descend through localization, and use resolutions to prove invertibility and the counit square on every homotopy object. Extensionality on the resolving class proves uniqueness from the required K-flat normalization.

The ordinary augmentation square commutes because both sides send x to the inverse image of 1 tensor x. Apply the exact-localization factorization to this square and the two universal reduction counits. At a K-flat source its counit is invertible; the normalized pullback comparison implies invertibility of the whole target factor needed for cancellation. Cancel it to obtain the derived augmentation/pullback square, then extend equality to every derived object using K-flat resolutions. Naturality of adjunction mates, together with the proved identification of chi as the mate of the diagonal pullback square, gives the required projection/augmentation equation.

proof_origin.place: D9: complete Lean proofs using Tags 06YS, 07A4 and 0B56, derived.tex Tags 08BJ and 070K, and the universal-unit/mate formulas for constant towers and limits. The four original conclusions and the unit route are retained. The ordinary and derived comparison existence/uniqueness obligations are proved, and the final normalization follows from the augmentation square and mate naturality. Generic categorical arguments replace the planned diagram-site and abstract projection-mate detour.

The split constructs the diagonal derived direct-image isomorphism on the diagram site, checks its evaluation and derived-limit normalization on K-injective representatives, constructs the quotient-tower projection mate by the ringed-site counit-tensor formula, and proves the augmentation equation by its unit normalization. Generic ringed-topos projection mate supplies the counit-tensor map, naturality, and tensor-unit normalization used to define h and prove clause (4).
Generic derived tensor/pullback comparison identifies the diagram-site tensor used in the projection mate with the specified reduction tower.
Generic K-injective preservation by a right adjoint to an exact functor justifies the diagonal K-injective representative.
Generic existence of K-injective resolutions is used to choose the representative for the unbounded derived direct image.
Generic total-derived-functor computation on K-injectives identifies the literal diagonal direct image with R_f^T.
Generic K-flat resolution is used to realize the quotient tensor tower strictly before localization.
Generic exact inverse image for arbitrary constant rings identifies coefficient pullbacks and makes direct image preserve K-injectives; finite-ring specializations do not cover A.

lean.statement: theorem constantTowerDirectImageNormalization (d : CompleteCoefficientDatum A) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : IsDirectImageNormalizedOnKInjectives (moduleDirectImage A f) (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : Modules A X ⥤ Towers A X) (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : Modules A Y ⥤ Towers A Y) (towerDirectImage A f) (Functor.compConstIso ℕᵒᵖ (moduleDirectImage A f)) (chi A f) ∧ (∀ (M : DerivedCategory (Modules A X)) (n : ℕ), (ev A Y n).map ((chi A f).hom.app M) ≫ (evalR A f n).app ((delta A X).obj M) ≫ (push A f).map ((deltaEval A X n).hom.app M) = (deltaEval A Y n).hom.app ((push A f).obj M)) ∧ (∀ M : DerivedCategory (Modules A X), (push A f).map ((deltaLimit A X).inv.app M) ≫ (limitPush A f).hom.app ((delta A X).obj M) ≫ (L A Y).map ((chi A f).inv.app M) ≫ (deltaLimit A Y).hom.app ((push A f).obj M) = 𝟙 _) ∧ (∀ M : DerivedCategory (Modules A X), (augmentation d.ideal Y).app ((push A f).obj M) ≫ (projection d.ideal f).app M = (chi A f).hom.app M ≫ (R A f).map ((augmentation d.ideal X).app M))
